rationale: Correct Ontario Science Partners to its legal ProjectCo identity and remove the false JLIL/Equitix attribution. Direct 2026 evidence establishes a 64% John Laing, 26% Sacyr Infrastructure Canada and 10% Amico Major Projects sponsor split at financial close. Because the 2021 takeover terms reserved future John Laing investments to KKR, the 64% John Laing interest is represented once under KKR with its direct holding vehicle, not duplicated as a separate John Laing and KKR stake.

beforeImage.subsector: DBFM cultural and science centre infrastructure
beforeImage.description: Ontario Science Partners is the consortium selected to deliver the new Ontario Science Centre project at Ontario Place. Its end user is the public sector and the visiting public, with economics structured through a design-build-finance-maintain concession rather than commercial admissions risk. The project is asset-heavy and still in the pre-construction phase following contract award in 2026. Public sources identify the scope as a new science centre facility together with rehabilitation of the Cinesphere and Pods. The reviewed materials did not disclose project-level revenue or financing beyond the announced procurement structure. Infrastructure Ontario and John Laing disclosed in February 2026 that the Ontario Science Partners consortium consists of John Laing at 64%, Sacyr Infrastructure Canada at 26%, and Amico Major Projects at 10%.

afterImage.name: Ontario Science Partners General Partnership
afterImage.subsector: DBFM cultural and science centre infrastructure
afterImage.description: Ontario Science Partners General Partnership is the ProjectCo delivering the new Ontario Science Centre at Ontario Place in Toronto under a C$1.04 billion design-build-finance-maintain concession. The approximately 400,000-square-foot scope includes the new centre and rehabilitation of the Cinesphere and Pods, followed by a 30-year maintenance term. The ProjectCo reached financial close on February 11, 2026 with John Laing holding 64%, Sacyr Infrastructure Canada 26% and Amico Major Projects 10%. John Laing's interest is attributed to KKR because the 2021 takeover terms reserved all future John Laing investments to KKR; the project is outside the legacy JLIL/Equitix portfolio. Construction began in May 2026 with opening targeted for 2029, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.
